Infra map

How Bunkai TMS is built and the non-functional budgets it holds, reverse-engineered from the product code of upex-bunkai-tms at main commit e88512e (read-only snapshot). Paths are relative to that repo. Phase 2 sections (architecture, external services, NFRs) are below; the Phase 3 sections (backend, frontend, environments, CI/CD) are added by project-discovery Phase 3. Design-time intent from the target .context/SRS/ is quoted only where labelled as intent: it is not evidence of implementation.

Overview

Bunkai is a single Next.js App Router application that serves both the web UI and a versioned REST API (app/api/v1/**) from one deployable, backed entirely by Supabase (Postgres with Row Level Security, plus Supabase Auth). There is no separate backend service, no ORM, no queue and no cache tier: server components, one Server Action and the route handlers talk to Supabase directly through @supabase/ssr / @supabase/supabase-js. Multi-row writes go through Postgres functions (bunkai_* RPCs). The pattern is a feature-light modular monolith: app/ owns routing and pages, lib/api/ the API cross-cutting concerns (auth, error envelope, logging, idempotency), lib/supabase/ the data clients, and supabase/migrations/ the schema, policies and functions.

Containers and data flow

  • Browser → Middleware → App UI: page requests pass the middleware (session refresh against Supabase Auth via getUser), then server components query Postgres with the user's JWT, so RLS decides what rows come back.
  • App UI → Postgres: reads through the server client; the ATC save is the Server Action calling the bunkai_save_atc RPC (SECURITY INVOKER, one transaction, RLS evaluated as the caller).
  • Browser → Middleware → Route handlers: client components call /api/v1/* with fetch and the session cookie (onboarding, workspace switcher, members, invite accept, magic-link form).
  • CLI / agent / test → Route handlers: Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_*. The middleware still runs on these requests but only refreshes cookies.
  • Route handlers → Postgres: either the user-scoped server client (RLS applies) or the service-role admin client (RLS bypassed; used for PAT lookup, PAT minting, idempotency rows, invite secrets, invite acceptance, and the Bearer branch of GET /workspaces and GET /me).
  • Route handlers → Supabase Auth: signInWithOtp, signInWithPassword, auth.admin.createUser, auth.admin.getUserById.

Auth flow

Three entry paths, all ending in a Supabase user id:

  1. Magic link (UI): the login form posts the email to POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link → signInWithOtp with emailRedirectTo = {app url}/auth/callback?next=… → Supabase Auth emails the link → GET /auth/callback?code=… exchanges the code for a session and sets the sb-* auth cookies → redirect to next (default /projects). A best-effort audit row goes to magic_link_tokens + magic_link_token_secrets.
  2. Headless sign-up / sign-in (API): POST /api/v1/auth/signup creates the user with email_confirm: true through the admin API (no confirmation email), signs in with the password to set session cookies on the response, and mints a PAT; POST /api/v1/auth/signin does the same for an existing user. Both return the Supabase session tokens and the PAT once.
  3. PAT on later calls: requireBearerToken parses bk_pat_{12-char prefix}.{rest}, looks up access_tokens by prefix, compares SHA-256 against access_token_secrets, rejects revoked or expired tokens with a uniform 401, and fire-and-forgets last_used_at.

Which endpoints accept which credential (from the handlers at e88512e): only GET /api/v1/workspaces and GET /api/v1/me call the dual-mode requireAuth and accept a PAT. Every other authenticated handler (POST /workspaces, GET|PATCH /workspaces/{id}, invites, invites/accept, tokens, me/active-workspace) reads the cookie session only, so a PAT alone gets a 401 there. Scopes (atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin) are stored on the token, but no handler calls requireScope / requireScopeOrCookie: scopes are not enforced yet.

Database at architecture level

One store: Supabase Postgres, reached through PostgREST via @supabase/supabase-js (no ORM, no direct SQL connection from the app). Subsystems by migration: tenancy (workspaces, members), projects and modules, authoring (user stories, acceptance criteria), ATCs (header, steps, assertions, AC anchoring, full-text tsv maintained by a trigger), access tokens, cross-cutting (idempotency keys, activity log, feature flags, view state, magic-link audit), workspace invites, and secret side-tables split out so QA inspection roles cannot read hashes. Tables, columns and lifecycles belong to business-data-context (bun run context:map business-data-context); the vocabulary is in business-domain-context (term-* sections). Generated types live in lib/types/supabase.ts.

Security architecture

  • AuthN: Supabase Auth JWT in sb-* cookies for browsers; PATs (SHA-256 of the secret stored, only the 12-char prefix in clear) for API callers.
  • AuthZ: Row Level Security on every table; membership checks centralised in SECURITY DEFINER helpers (bunkai_is_workspace_member, bunkai_can_write_workspace, bunkai_is_workspace_admin, bunkai_is_workspace_owner, search_path = ''). Roles: viewer < member < admin < owner. Workspace bootstrap is the SECURITY DEFINER RPC bunkai_bootstrap_workspace, executable by authenticated.
  • Service-role bypass: the admin client skips RLS; handlers that use it check authorization in code (e.g. invite accept checks status, expiry and invitee email; the Bearer branch of GET /workspaces joins on membership).
  • Secrets at rest: PAT, magic-link and invite secrets hashed in *_secrets tables revoked from anon, authenticated, qa_inspector_ro, qa_inspector_rw.
  • Idempotency: lib/api/idempotency.ts implements Idempotency-Key replay over the idempotency_keys table, but no route calls it at e88512e.

Performance hooks

No cache layer and no rate limiter in the app. revalidatePath after the ATC save; force-static + Cache-Control on the OpenAPI spec; a GIN-indexed tsvector on ATCs. Supabase's own OTP rate limit surfaces as 429 on the magic-link route. Details in nfr-performance.

ADRs

  • .context/ADR/ADR-0009-auth-in-tests-headless-signup-pat.md (Proposed): tests get identity through the headless signup / signin endpoints, cookie session vs PAT chosen per endpoint, magic link only in its own tests.
  • .context/ADR/ADR-0010-test-isolation-user-workspace-under-rls.md (Proposed): mutating tests isolate data by owning a fresh user + workspace, relying on RLS tenancy.

QA relevance

  • Test RLS as a first-class surface: cross-workspace reads and writes per role, through both the UI path (cookie) and the API path (cookie and PAT).
  • The cookie-only vs PAT-capable split decides how API tests authenticate; a PAT-only API client cannot reach most endpoints today.
  • Magic-link login needs a reachable inbox and is subject to Supabase's OTP rate limit: keep it out of per-test setup.
  • Selectors: data-testid exists only on the login form and the /qa page; the authenticated app has none (see discovery-gaps).

Backend

The backend is the server half of the single Next.js app: Route Handlers under app/api/v1/**, one Server Action, server components, and Supabase (Postgres + Auth) reached over HTTP. No separate service, no ORM, no Docker.

Local development setup

# 1. Install dependencies
bun install

# 2. Environment: .env.example is NOT sufficient on its own (see the table above)
cp .env.example .env
#    then set at least:
#    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY

# 3. Database: no local Supabase stack and no migrate/seed command in the repo.
#    Point the keys at an existing Supabase project whose schema matches supabase/migrations/.
#    Optional, after a schema change on that project:
bun run types:gen

# 4. Start the dev server (http://localhost:3000)
bun run dev

# 5. Verify (liveness only, does not touch the database)
curl http://localhost:3000/api/v1/health

# Build and serve like production
bun run build
bun run start

Test and quality commands

The product has no automated tests: no test runner, no test script, no test files under app/, components/ or lib/. The only gates are type check and lint, run by git hooks (details in ci-cd): 

bun run typecheck
bun run lint:check
bun run openapi:gen   # then check git diff on public/openapi.json

Headless sign-inPOST /api/v1/auth/signin, same body200; uniform 401 for unknown email or wrong passwordSame as sign-upapp/api/v1/auth/signin/route.ts
PAT from a cookie sessionPOST /api/v1/tokens { scopes, name?, workspace_id?, expires_in_days? } with the session cookie201PATapp/api/v1/tokens/route.ts
API call with PATAuthorization: Bearer bk_pat_{12-char prefix}.{rest}Accepted only by GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/workspaces-lib/api/auth.ts, lib/api/middleware/bearer.ts
 
# Sign-up / sign-in body (password 6 to 128 chars, email max 254)
{ "email": "...", "password": "...",
  "pat_name": "optional, 1-80 chars",          # default "cli-signup" / "cli-signin"
  "pat_scopes": ["atc:read","atc:write","run:execute","workspace:admin"],  # default: all four
  "pat_expires_in_days": 7 }                   # optional, 1-365; omitted = never expires

# Response body (201 signup / 200 signin)
{ "user":    { "id": "<uuid>", "email": "..." },
  "session": { "access_token", "refresh_token", "expires_at", "token_type" },
  "pat":     { "token": "bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>", "id", "name", "scopes", "expires_at" },
  "warning": "Store the PAT token now — it cannot be retrieved later." }
# plus Set-Cookie: sb-<project-ref>-auth-token... (Supabase SSR cookies)
  • The UI offers magic link only; there is no password field. A user created through the magic link has no password, so signin cannot authenticate it (the /qa guide says the same).
  • The Supabase access_token is not accepted as a Bearer: requireBearerToken rejects anything not starting with bk_pat_. Cookie-only endpoints need the sb-* cookies.
  • signup uses the service-role admin API with email_confirm: true, so it sends no email; every signin mints a new PAT row.
  • The session cookie name embeds the Supabase project ref, so it differs per environment; the browser receives it for the app's own host only.
  • Health: GET /api/v1/health (liveness, no DB). Discovery banner: GET /api/v1. Spec: GET /api/openapi, whose paths carry the full /api/v1/… prefix and whose servers are bare hosts.

Test-architecture decisions built on this contract: ADR-0009 (headless signup / signin, both credentials) and ADR-0010 (fresh user + workspace per mutating test).

Rendering model

  • React Server Components for every authenticated page under app/(app)/: they read Supabase with the cookie session (RLS applies) and redirect to /login when there is no user.
  • Client components ('use client') for interactive parts: login form, onboarding form, members, invite accept, ATC editor and table, layout shell, auth provider. They call /api/v1/* with fetch and the session cookie.
  • One Server Action: saveAtcAction (ATC save) followed by revalidatePath.
  • Middleware refreshes the session on every non-static request and redirects anonymous users from /projects* and /onboarding*. / redirects to /login.
  • Theme is dark only (dark class fixed on the root element; Tailwind darkMode: ['class']).

Styling and component library

  • Tailwind CSS 3 with CSS-variable design tokens (tailwind.config.ts, app/globals.css); token spec in DESIGN.md.
  • shadcn/ui configuration, style new-york, RSC on, lucide icons (components.json); primitives in components/ui/: badge, button, card, input, label, tabs. Built on Radix (dialog, dropdown-menu, tabs, tooltip) with class-variance-authority and tailwind-merge.
  • Feature libraries: TanStack Table (components/atcs/AtcTable.tsx), Monaco loaded via next/dynamic (components/atcs/StepEditor.tsx), cmdk command palette (components/layout/CommandPalette.tsx), sonner toasts (Toaster top-right in app/layout.tsx).
  • Fonts: Inter, JetBrains Mono, Noto Serif JP via next/font/google.

State, data fetching and auth integration

  • No global store and no fetching library (no Redux, Zustand, TanStack Query or SWR): server components query Supabase, client components use fetch + useState.
  • AuthProvider (components/providers/auth-context.tsx) wraps app/(app)/layout.tsx and tracks the Supabase session with onAuthStateChange on the browser client.
  • Active workspace persists in the bk_active_ws cookie, switched through POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace from the workspace switcher.
  • Client env vars: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (plus the unused NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL). No secret-looking name carries the public prefix.

Static assets and SEO

public/ holds only openapi.json: no favicon, robots.txt or sitemap. No next/image usage. Root metadata sets the title and a metadataBase hard-coded to http://localhost:3000 in every environment. Bundle size is not measured (see nfr-performance).

Test-ID strategy

  • data-testid exists in two places only, kebab-case and area-prefixed: the login form (login-email, login-submit) and the /qa page (qa-page, qa-title, qa-credentials-card, qa-credentials-button, qa-docs-button, qa-db-ways, qa-api-ways, qa-auth-methods, qa-env-setup, qa-code-block, qa-copy-code-button, qa-agent-tabs, qa-toc, qa-toc-link-{id}, qa-architecture-diagram, qa-repos).
  • Zero data-testid in components/ and the authenticated pages; almost no aria-* attributes and no explicit role= attributes in app or components.
  • Workable today: role and accessible-name locators that come from native elements and Radix primitives (buttons with visible text, inputs wrapped in a label element on the login form), plus the two login test IDs. A selector contract for the app is a team decision (see discovery-gaps).

Internationalization

None: no i18n library, lang="en" on the root element, English strings hard-coded in components. Only the /qa guide content is written in Spanish.

bun install
bun run dev        # http://localhost:3000 → redirects to /login
bun run build
bun run start

Monitoring and rollback

  • Monitoring: only the JSON access log on stdout (lib/api/logging.ts), visible wherever Vercel keeps function logs. No error tracking, uptime monitor or APM (nfr-observability).
  • Rollback: no procedure in the repo. App code can only roll back through the hosting platform; schema changes are forward-only SQL with no down scripts, so a DB rollback needs a hand-written reverse migration or a Supabase backup restore.

QA relevance

  • Run against staging by default; never write to production.
  • Auth cookies are named per Supabase project ref, so a storageState captured on one environment is useless on another.
  • Magic-link and invite URLs are built from APP_URLS, not from the request host: a test on a preview or a non-3000 local port follows links to another host.

CI/CD

CI pipelines

None in the repo. No .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, CircleCI, Azure or Jenkins config. No pipeline runs tests, because there are no tests. The only automated gates are local git hooks (husky), which a developer can skip with --no-verify:

HookRuns
pre-commitbunx lint-staged (eslint --fix on TS/JS, prettier --write on JSON/YAML/CSS/HTML), bun run types:check, vars:check, skills:check, and skills:registry:check when skill files are staged
pre-pushbun run repo:check (format, lint, types, vars, vars:env, skills, skills registry)

Of those, only lint, prettier and tsc touch the product; the rest checks the inherited boilerplate. Nothing checks that public/openapi.json matches the route definitions (it is regenerated by hand with bun run openapi:gen).

Deployment

  • Target: Vercel, inferred from VERCEL_ENV handling in lib/urls.ts, .vercel in .gitignore and the Vercel notes in .env.example.
  • No vercel.json: build, install and output settings are Vercel's Next.js defaults or live in the Vercel dashboard. Whether deploys come from the Vercel git integration, and from which branches, is unverified.
  • No Dockerfile, Compose file or other host config.

Database migrations

No migration pipeline: no Supabase CLI config, no apply script, no workflow. How supabase/migrations/*.sql reach each Supabase project, and in what order relative to the app deploy, is undocumented. .env.example names a SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN for the Supabase MCP "migrations" capability, which hints that migrations are applied by hand or by an agent; unverified.

Infrastructure as code

Not present (no Terraform, Pulumi, CDK or Serverless files).

Deployment checklist (derived; nothing in the repo enforces it)

  • Pre-deploy: bun run typecheck, bun run lint:check, bun run openapi:gen with no diff, migrations applied to the target Supabase project before code that depends on them ships.
  • Post-deploy: GET /api/v1/health answers ok; /login renders; a headless signin returns 200.
  • Rollback: revert the app through Vercel; reverse migrations by hand (see environments).

QA relevance

  • This QA repo's own CI workflows would be the first automated test job for the product. Nothing links a product deploy to a QA run (no deploy webhook or status check), so regression runs are triggered by hand or on schedule.
  • Staging can change without notice: there is no deploy log in the repo to correlate a failure with a release.

Discovery gaps

  • Compliance: no GDPR, SOC 2 or data-export / deletion implementation in code (the SRS places it on a Phase 3 horizon). Needs review; not implemented.
  • Rate limiting: no app-level limiter. The magic-link OpenAPI description names a Supabase free-tier OTP limit; the actual limit of each Supabase project is unverified. SRS intent of per-token limits is not implemented.
  • Performance numbers: no latency, throughput or bundle-size measurement exists; SRS budgets are intent only.
  • Accessibility: SRS targets WCAG 2.1 AA; not verified from code in this phase.
  • Selector contract: data-testid appears only in app/(auth)/login/magic-link-form.tsx and app/qa/; none in components/ or the authenticated pages. No convention to record as an ADR yet; ask the team whether one will be adopted.
  • Signup endpoint in production: whether POST /api/v1/auth/signup is reachable on production and intended to be is unknown (affects ADR-0009 and ADR-0010).
  • Data cleanup: no API deletes users, workspaces or projects; how test data is purged on staging is undecided.
  • Supabase project settings: SMTP provider, OTP limits, JWT expiry, password policy and backups are set in the Supabase dashboard, not in the repo. Source: Supabase project owner.
  • Unused schema: activity_log, feature_flags, user_view_state and the idempotency helper have no product callers at e88512e; confirm whether they are planned or dead.
  • Monaco CDN: the editor's runtime asset source is inferred from the library default, not observed; an offline or CSP-restricted environment could break the editor.
  • API contract drift: the served spec (generated from route.openapi.ts) and the design-time .context/SRS/api-contracts.yaml were not compared; spot-check before relying on either (bun run api:sync, then project-context mode api).
  • Diagram style: no .diagram-design marker at the QA repo root; the figure uses diagram-design's default skin, which matches this map's palette. A team skin can be chosen later.
  • Runtime version: no Node.js version is pinned (no .nvmrc, .node-version or engines); the version Vercel builds with is unknown. Source: Vercel project settings.
  • Local bootstrap: .env.example lacks the two keys lib/env.ts requires (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY), so a fresh clone does not boot from it; which Supabase project local development should use is undocumented. Source: target maintainers.
  • Migration workflow: no Supabase CLI config, apply script, seed or pipeline; how and when supabase/migrations/ reach each environment, and whether staging and production share one Supabase project, is unknown. Source: Supabase project owner.
  • Deploy mechanics: staging is inferred to run as VERCEL_ENV=preview; its branch, the production branch, whether the Vercel git integration deploys automatically and whether per-PR previews exist are unverified. Source: Vercel project settings.
  • Production liveness: https://upexbunkai.vercel.app is in code but was not contacted (no network calls in discovery). Source: Vercel project owner.
  • Hard-coded URLs: redirect and invite links use APP_URLS by VERCEL_ENV, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is validated but unused, and metadataBase is localhost everywhere. Confirm whether this is intended before testing previews or a non-default local port.
  • API base path for the test client: the OpenAPI servers are bare hosts with /api/v1/… paths, environments.*.api_url in .agents/project.yaml ends in /api, and the /qa guide uses /api/v1 as API_BASE_URL. /test-framework-adaptation must pick one convention.
  • CI, monitoring, rollback: no CI, no deploy-to-QA trigger, no monitoring beyond stdout logs and no rollback runbook exist in the repo; confirm whether any live outside it (Vercel dashboard, Supabase backups). Source: target maintainers.
  • Inspector roles: the /qa page describes qa_inspector_ro / qa_inspector_rw as BYPASSRLS; their existence and grants per environment are unverified, and DB-level checks through them cannot prove RLS behaviour.
